content.text: No renewal or price-uplift mechanic exists anywhere; the Term is a self-expiring royalty-term construct.

input.quote: 12.1 Term. The term of this Agreement shall commence upon the Effective Date and, unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Article XII, shall continue in full force and effect until the expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement, whichever is later (the "Term").
input.rationale: The Term runs from the Effective Date until expiration of Sanofi's payment obligations under Article IX or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement (Section 12.1), with duration driven by the Royalty Term on a Product-by-Product/country-by-country basis (Section 9.3(b)) and the Profit/Loss Share Agreement running to expiry of that Royalty Term (Section 9.4). Searches for "renew", "automatically renew", extension, and CPI/price-increase language return no renewal mechanic anywhere in the Agreement (the only "non-renewal" hits are the insurance-notice provision at p0603 and a force majeure example at p0606, neither of which is a term renewal). Because renewal is not automatic and no renewal price uplift exists, both fallback elements are satisfied vacuously and there is no notice window to shorten or uplift to cap. Sanofi also holds a broad convenience termination right under Section 12.2(a)(i), so exit is not constrained by any renewal cycle. Inserting an auto-renewal or opt-out mechanic would add structure that does not exist and would not benefit us; no redline is warranted. Noted only for the record: the rule's preferred parameters (12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder, CPI/3% cap) are simply inapplicable to this royalty-term-based collaboration structure rather than absent from a renewal bargain.
